questions.q: What is data provenance, as defined in this lesson?
options: A tracked record of where training data came from, who touched it, and when
A compression format for large training datasets
A cryptographic algorithm used only for model weights, not datasets
A type of adversarial example used to test model robustness
questions.explain: Data provenance means tracking the origin and history of training data so unexplained or unauthorized changes become visible instead of silently flowing into a training run.

questions.q: What does dataset versioning, using tools like DVC, lakeFS, or MLflow, let a team do?
options: Automatically encrypt all training data at rest
Delete old training runs to save storage space
See exactly what changed between one training run's data and the next, similar to a git diff for code
Bypass the need for any data validation step entirely
questions.explain: Dataset versioning treats data like source code — versioned and diffable — so unexpected statistical shifts between versions become visible before training even starts.

questions.q: What is the role of TensorFlow Data Validation (TFDV) and Great Expectations in a real ML pipeline?
options: They train the model directly on labeled data
They replace the need for a held-out validation set
They are only used for generating model cards, not for checking data
They automatically check a dataset's schema and statistics before training, flagging drift and anomalies
questions.explain: TFDV and Great Expectations validate a dataset's shape and statistics against expectations, failing the pipeline automatically when a batch looks anomalous, whether from an attacker or an upstream bug.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend keeping an untouched holdout validation set?
options: It is required by law in every jurisdiction
It gives a clean baseline to evaluate against, including for the backdoor-detection techniques covered earlier in this chapter
It removes the need for any dataset versioning
It is the only way to load a pretrained model safely
questions.explain: A holdout set the data pipeline never writes to provides a clean, trustworthy baseline to evaluate a model against, supporting techniques like activation clustering and Neural Cleanse from Lesson 11.

questions.q: According to this lesson's closing checklist, who should be covered by access-control review in a training data pipeline?
options: Only the data scientists who built the original model
Anyone who can modify training data, the same as any other sensitive system
No one, since training data is considered public by default
Only external auditors hired after a model has already shipped
questions.explain: The lesson's checklist treats write access to training data as a credential that access-control review must cover, since anyone who can modify it can influence what the model learns.
